subject.title: [Security] Mitigating timing attacks in GitHub Auth OAuth callback validation

question: After checking shipped GitHub authentication paths, should this public report be closed as targeting nonexistent code or retained for deeper private investigation?
rationale: Current main does not contain the reported boundary, but the protected security labels require an authorized human to confirm shipped behavior and choose the disclosure disposition.

options.title: Close and redirect privately
options.body: Close the public issue after confirming shipped releases also use device-code polling, and invite a private advisory only if a concrete reachable callback path can be demonstrated.

options.title: Audit shipped authentication paths
options.body: Keep the issue open temporarily while an authorized security reviewer searches release tags and historical GitHub-auth implementations for an alternate callback route.

recommendation.title: Close and redirect privately
recommendation.body: Close the public issue after confirming shipped releases also use device-code polling, and invite a private advisory only if a concrete reachable callback path can be demonstrated.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is recent authorship of both shared comparison and gateway authentication hardening changes.
